items.text: India is launching an AI lab into space today: Here's what it is
items.article: TakeMe2Space's MOI-1A is set to launch aboard SpaceX's Falcon 9 as an orbital computing satellite. The mission will test whether AI can process Earth-observation data in orbit before transmission. Imagine a satellite looking down at Earth, capturing thousands of images, but instead of sending all that data back to a computer on Earth, it stops, thinks and sends back only what matters. That is the idea behind MOI-1A, an orbital computing satellite being developed by Hyderabad-based startup TakeMe2Space. The spacecraft is scheduled to launch on October 1 aboard SpaceX’s Falcon 9 as part of the Transporter-18 rideshare mission. The company describes it as India’s first orbital computing satellite. So, what exactly does an “AI lab in space” mean? Today, satellites can collect enormous amounts of information, from images of farms and forests to observations of infrastructure and ships. Traditionally, much of that information has to be transmitted to Earth, where computers analyse it. That process takes time and requires considerable communication bandwidth.
